title: cross-boundary envelope
description: Every cross-boundary message is wrapped in this envelope. Owning protocol: Protocol Index Section 6. The envelope is a wrapper, not a wire surface: it carries the `surface` of the message it carries, and `serea.envelope/1` is not a registered surface. This is a forward-compatible surface: undeclared fields are preserved verbatim in the host's opaque extension set and round-tripped unchanged (Protocol Index Section 4.2 rule 3 and Section 5), so this document declares no additionalProperties: false at the object level.

message_id.description: This message's own identity. Delivery is at-least-once; recipients deduplicate by this value.

correlation_id.description: Follows the causal chain of the task. Absent only when the message is not task-scoped.

causation_id.description: Names the specific message that caused this one. Absent only for user-originated messages.

data_class.description: The producer's declared class for payload. A consumer that computes a higher class must treat the payload as the higher class (Data Classification Section 1).

payload.description: The message body. Its shape belongs to the owning surface's schema; the host validates it against that closed schema before any authority decision (Protocol Index Section 4.2 rule 3).

envelopeVersion.description: Decimal envelope major with no leading zero.

timestamp.description: The syntactic form only. ECMA-262 regular expressions have no date arithmetic, so a calendar-impossible but well-formed value such as 2026-02-30T00:00:00Z passes this pattern; the Rust Timestamp value is the authority for calendar validity and refuses it. Every value Serea puts on the wire is deserialised into that type.

trace.description: Correlation context. Forward-compatible like the envelope that contains it: correlation carries no authority, and Protocol Index Section 4.1 makes a new optional member an architecture-minor change.
